newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST-Taiwan January CPI - Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Taiwan January CPI - Reuters poll.

text.p: The following Reuters poll of economists gives their year-on-year projections for Taiwan's consumer price index in January.
The official figures were scheduled to be issued at 0300 GMT on February 5 by the cabinet's Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics.
December's CPI growth was 2.52 percent year-on-year and CPI growth for the whole of 1996 was 3.07 percent.
The poll results produced an average forecast for a rise of 3.18 percent in annual CPI growth in January.

Economists said an average nine percent domestic oil product price increase by state-run monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp from January 1 would add some 0.387 percentage points to the January consumer price index.
"January's CPI growth should be comparatively high because of the domestic oil price hikes," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.

HSBC James Capel economist Steven Wang pointed out two sectors that expected to counterbalance the energy price increases: "Vegetable prices are seen stable and garment prices should fall in January."
The cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development recently adopted a 1997 CPI growth target of 3.0 percent.
The council has failed to persuade the central bank to revise what it calls its more realistic 1997 CPI growth forecast of 3.31 percent.
